title: Memory vs Storage
about: Tell the desk from the cupboard, and spot when each one is full.

cards.prompt: Your laptop's battery dies without warning. When you charge it and switch it back on, what's **still there**? Think about what was **saved** and what was only **open**.

items.label: A photo you saved last week
An essay you hadn't saved yet
A half-played game level, not saved
A drawing you'd started but hadn't saved

cards.explanation: Saved and installed things live in **storage**, which keeps them with the power off. Anything that was only open lived in **RAM**, which is wiped when the power goes. (That's why many apps save your work for you every few minutes.)
cards.hint: For each one, ask: was it saved or installed, or was it only open on the screen?
cards.nudge: Saving is what keeps things safe. Anything that was only open, and never saved, doesn't survive the power going off.

cards.title: The desk and the cupboard
cards.body:
That's because a device has two kinds of space, both measured in gigabytes (**GB**).

**RAM** is the desk: fast but small. It holds whatever is open right now, and it's **cleared when the power goes off**.

**Storage** is the cupboard: bigger and slower. It keeps apps, photos and saved files until you delete them.

cards.prompt: This phone has **4 [[GB|gigabyte]] of RAM**. When the open apps need more than that, it starts to lag. Play the **racing game** with your **music** still on, and get it running **smoothly**. (The phone's own system always needs some RAM too.)
cards.explanation: Every open app needs room in **RAM**. With the game added, the apps needed 5.8 GB, more than the phone's 4 GB, so it lagged. Closing the [[browser]] and the video call made room for the game and the music. (A laptop with full RAM slows down instead, as it shuffles things out to storage.)
cards.hint: Every open app takes room in RAM. The game and the music must stay on, so which apps don't you need?
cards.nudge: If it still lags, the open apps need more room than the phone's 4 GB of RAM. Keep the game and music on, and close what you don't need.

cards.title: A real RAM stick

photo.alt: A green laptop RAM stick with a label in the middle, black memory chips and a row of gold contacts along its bottom edge.

cards.caption: A laptop RAM stick (8 GB). The gold contacts along the bottom plug into a slot. In phones and many thin laptops, the RAM chips are soldered straight onto the board instead.

cards.prompt: Downloads are saved in **[[storage]]**. Your laptop has **20 [[GB|gigabyte]] free**. Sort each download: does it fit on its own?
cards.explanation: Anything up to 20 GB fits. The 21 GB game misses by just 1 GB, and the series and the racing game are far too big. [[RAM]] makes no difference: a download needs free storage.
cards.hint: Compare each size with the 20 GB you have free.
cards.nudge: Only free storage counts here. Anything bigger than 20 GB won't fit, even if it's only a little bigger.

cards.prompt: You're about to take a photo of a rainbow, and a message pops up.

steps.text: **"Not enough space. Can't save photo."** Which kind of space has run out?

choices.consequence: Right. Saving a photo needs room in storage, and yours is full.
RAM only holds what's running right now. A photo you *save* goes to storage, and that's what's full.

steps.text: The rainbow won't last long. How do you make room quickly?

choices.consequence: That frees **RAM**, not storage. The message comes straight back.

choices.text: Delete big videos you've backed up (copied somewhere else)
choices.consequence: Videos take up lots of storage, so deleting a few you've backed up frees plenty of room. You get the shot!
Restarting clears RAM, but every file in storage is still there. It's still full.

cards.explanation: A "not enough space" message when you **save** something means **storage** is full. Only removing files frees storage. Closing apps and restarting only clear RAM.
cards.hint: The message appeared when you tried to save a photo. Which kind of space keeps saved files?

cards.prompt: A laptop has been on for weeks and feels slow. Why does restarting it often help?

options.text: It empties RAM, clearing out what apps left behind
It clears out old files you no longer need from storage
options.nudge: Restarting doesn't touch storage: every file is still there afterwards. Think about which space is cleared when the power goes off.

options.text: It resets the CPU so it can run at a higher speed again
options.nudge: A restart doesn't change the CPU at all. Think about the desk: what happens to it when the power goes off?

options.text: It gives the laptop more RAM than it had before
options.nudge: The amount of RAM is fixed by the parts inside, so a restart can't add any. Think about what happens to what's already in it.

cards.explanation: Turning off clears **RAM**, including leftovers from apps that didn't tidy up after themselves. Your files in **storage** stay exactly where they were, and the amount of RAM never changes.
cards.hint: Which kind of space does a restart affect?

cards.prompt: You're choosing a new laptop for video editing. More [[RAM]] costs more money. Pick the **smallest** amount of RAM that runs everything **smoothly**.
cards.explanation: The system and the three apps need 2 + 3 + 1.5 + 0.5 = **7 [[GB|gigabyte]]**. The smallest choice that fits is **8 GB**. Anything more works too, but costs more than you need.
cards.hint: Keep all three apps open. Watch the RAM needed meter, then find the smallest amount of RAM that fits it.
cards.nudge: All three apps must stay open. Too little RAM and it lags; too much costs more than you need. Look for the smallest setting that runs smoothly.

cards.prompt: Your phone has **40 [[GB|gigabyte]] of free storage**, but something's wrong.

steps.text: Every time you switch back to the game, it **starts loading from scratch**, and the music app keeps stopping. What's running short?

choices.consequence: Yes. When RAM fills up, the phone closes apps in the background to make room, so they have to reload.
There's 40 GB free, so storage isn't the problem. Apps reloading is a sign the **workspace** is full.

steps.text: What's the best fix for right now?

choices.text: Close the apps you aren't using
choices.consequence: That frees RAM for the game and the music. They stop reloading.
Photos live in storage, which had plenty of room. RAM is still just as full.
That's one more app filling RAM, and "booster" apps are often junk or worse.

cards.explanation: Apps that keep **reloading** are a sign of full **RAM**, not full storage. Closing apps you aren't using gives the others room. Deleting files only frees storage.
cards.hint: Notice there's 40 GB of storage free. Think back to what a phone does when its desk gets full.

cards.title: Recap
cards.body:
- **RAM** is the fast desk for what's open. Power off clears it.
- **Storage** keeps apps and files until you delete them.
- Full RAM? Close apps. Full storage? Delete files you've [[backed up|backup]].

Next: the [[CPU]], the part that does the work.
